He said he would look at it. He agreed to deliver it. Is that the same thing?

Two things about recap emails, and they are the two that people get wrong. The first is that a recap is not a transcript. Nobody wants to know what was said. They want to know what was decided, who is doing what, and by when. If your email is longer than the meeting felt, you have written the wrong thing. The second one matters more. When you report what somebody else said, be careful with the verb you choose, because the verb is your judgement and everybody reads it as one. He said he would look at it is not the same as he agreed to deliver it, and he promised is not the same as he mentioned. I have seen a working relationship damaged by one word in a summary, where the meeting itself had been perfectly friendly. So report what was said, choose the verb that matches what was actually meant, and if you are not sure which verb that is, use said.

I write the recap in the same shape every single time, and it takes me about eight minutes. First line: what the meeting was about, in one sentence. Then, decisions. Not discussion, decisions. Then the actions, and every action has a name and a date, because an action without a name is a wish. Then anything that is still open, with the name of the person it is waiting for. And the last line is what I want them to remember if they read nothing else. When I report what somebody said, I keep it short and I keep it neutral. She said the invoice would arrive on Friday. He asked whether the forecast had been updated. They agreed to review it before the close. Three shapes, and they cover almost everything I ever need to write.
